Aldus FreeHand disk shipped MacMag virus

Target: Aldus FreeHand
Date: 1988-01-01 to 1988-03-02 (61 days)
Actor: Individual Hacker (person)
Target Kind: application
Language: N/A
Cause: insider_threat
Motive: vandalism_publicity
Transitive: false
Impact: nuisance
User Impact: 5000
Phase: distribution

Synopsis

Master copies of a promotional/training disk for Aldus FreeHand, a commercial graphics program, were infected with the MacMag virus by a contractor before duplication.

Story

Aldus FreeHand is one of the earliest clean examples of commercial software media carrying malware. The affected artifact was not the FreeHand application release in the abstract; it was a promotional or training floppy disk associated with the product, and the trusted path was physical duplication and magazine or customer distribution. That physical path matters. The user did not download a suspicious utility or accept a shareware copy. The disk arrived as part of a commercial software promotion, so the trust decision had already been made by the publisher's duplication process.

The malware was MacMag, also known as Drew, Brandow, Aldus, Peace, or World Peace. It targeted classic Macintosh systems, copied itself through the System folder path, and spread to bootable disks opened on an infected machine. Its intended behavior on March 2, 1988 was to display a "Universal Message of Peace" and then delete itself.

The payload was meant as nuisance and publicity, but bugs and context made it more serious. Public summaries describe crashes on some Mac II systems, possible accidental deletion in narrow cases, and broad user anxiety. Aldus had to recall thousands of FreeHand-related disks and threatened legal action after its media became a carrier.

This record is kept in scope because the malware moved through official commercial product media. It was not a random infected user disk; it was a contaminated master copied into a legitimate distribution channel.
